title: Chapter 7: Workshop Discipline and Safety Rules

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Always wear prescribed Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including safety shoes, goggles, and fitted clothing before entering the workshop.
Adhere strictly to the 5S housekeeping methodology: Sort (Seiri), Set in Order (Seiton), Shine (Seiso), Standardize (Seiketsu), and Sustain (Shitsuke).
Never operate any machine or power tool without formal authorization, proper safety instruction, and verified machine guards.
Inspect tools before use and never use defective or makeshift tools, such as files without handles or chisels with mushroomed heads.
Keep gangways, emergency exits, and fire extinguishers clear of scrap, tools, and oil spills at all times.

blocks.content: Workshop discipline refers to the set of rules, behaviors, and practices that workers must follow to maintain order, safety, and efficiency in a workshop or industrial environment. A disciplined workplace ensures that workers follow instructions, use tools properly, and maintain cleanliness and safety while performing technical tasks.

In technical trades such as fitting, welding, electrical work, and machining, proper discipline is essential because workers operate machines, tools, and electrical equipment that can be dangerous if used carelessly.

blocks.content: Safety in a workshop is not a set of rules to be memorized, but a discipline to be practiced every single minute.

items: Arrive on time and follow working hours
Wear appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Follow instructions given by supervisors or instructors
Use tools and machines only for their intended purpose
Keep the workplace clean and organized
Do not run or play inside the workshop
Avoid distractions while operating machines
Report damaged tools or unsafe conditions immediately

blocks.content: Housekeeping refers to maintaining cleanliness, order, and organization in the workplace. Good housekeeping practices reduce the risk of accidents and improve efficiency.

rows: Wearing fitted overalls, safety boots, and tucking in loose hair/sleeves
Wearing loose clothing, ties, wristwatches, or open sandals
Using the correct size tool in good condition with firm handles
Using mushroom-headed chisels, hammers with loose wedges, or files without handles
Ensuring guards are in place and stopping the machine before cleaning or adjusting
Cleaning swarf by hand while the machine is running or removing safety guards
Cleaning oil spills immediately and keeping walkways clear of obstacles
Leaving scrap metal, oily rags, and cables strewn across gangways

items: Always concentrate on the work being performed
Do not operate machines without training
Keep hands away from moving machine parts
Use machine guards and safety devices
Switch off machines before maintenance or adjustment

cells: Using the right tool prevents damage and injury

items: Check machine condition before starting work
Do not remove safety guards
Keep safe distance from moving parts
Stop machines immediately if abnormal noise occurs
Follow operating procedures strictly

Exam questions frequently test the 4 safety sign categories and their shapes/colors: Prohibition (Red circular), Mandatory (Blue circular), Warning (Yellow triangular), and Information/Safety (Green square/rectangular).
Be prepared for questions on the exact sequence and English/Japanese equivalents of the 5S housekeeping steps.
Tool safety questions commonly ask about the hazards of using a file without a ferrule/handle or using a mushroom-headed chisel.
